summary: Created the Fleet Internal CA on node1, installed it as trusted on both nodes, issued node2’s certificate, and configured persistent HTTPS on port 8443. Both nodes passed sequential restart and recovery verification without changing the OS release or kernel.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine-compatible OpenSSL and CA packages; installed nginx on node2.
Created the Fleet Internal CA and issued a node2 server certificate with DNS and managed-IP SANs.
Installed the CA into both system trust stores.
Configured and enabled nginx on node2 for TLS 1.2/1.3 on port 8443.
Verified trusted HTTPS locally and remotely.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA and issue node2 TLS certificate
evidence.summary: CA subject is CN=Fleet Internal CA. The node2 certificate chains successfully, has a matching private key, and contains DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.108.11 SANs.

evidence.requirement: Trust CA on both nodes and serve HTTPS on node2:8443
evidence.summary: Both system trust stores validated the certificate. nginx listened on port 8443 and returned HTTP 200 with the expected content.
Both nodes remained on Alpine Linux v3.23 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts after configuration and restarts.
Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 682c7814-666a-4071-a54c-056f9104ea3b to 1932bad1-da82-41e2-b085-c24ba3fa13f8; CA trust and remote HTTPS recovered.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 3725dbce-aa77-4c3d-bf21-e4baba5821bb to cc67ec2d-00bf-4a16-9a1e-c7ae339d938c; nginx, listener, certificates, trust, content, and remote HTTPS access recovered.
